comments.note: MovieEditorViewModel.cs: The DisposeImageViewModels method is now handling both image sub-VMs and the PlayerVm. A rename to DisposeSubViewModels would better reflect its expanded scope, but this is a low-priority readability matter.

MovieEditorView.axaml (Video tab): IsVisible='{Binding PlayerVm, Converter=...}' cannot share the same element as DataContext='{Binding PlayerVm}' in Avalonia compiled bindings — the compiler infers the DataContext type at the attribute level and resolves IsVisible against PlayerViewModel instead of MovieEditorViewModel. A Panel wrapper was used to keep the binding scopes separate. This is a recurring Avalonia compiled-binding pitfall worth documenting for future sub-VM views.

Program.cs: The MovieEditorViewModel DI factory lambda (lines 266-286) is growing in parameter count (now 15 args). Future WPs adding more optional services will make this unwieldy. Consider a parameter-object or builder pattern if more optional services are added.

comments.note: Renamed private method DisposeImageViewModels → DisposeSubViewModels and updated the XML summary docstring. The method now disposes ThumbnailsVm, CoverImageVm, GeneratorVm, AND PlayerVm — the old name only described the image sub-VMs, so it was misleading after the M9/M10 player wiring was added. All three call sites updated (declaration + 2 callers). Build confirmed clean after rename.
Removed 'M10' milestone prefix from the _playerFactory field comment (line 46). This factory is wired up in WP-029 which is part of the M9 plan; the milestone label was stale.

In LoadAsync, the call to DisposeSubViewModels() inside the image-services guard block (line ~653) already disposes PlayerVm, making the unconditional PlayerVm?.Dispose() at lines 697-698 redundant when image services are present. Both paths are safe (calling Dispose on null is a no-op) but the dual-disposal pattern is slightly confusing. The redundancy is harmless; a future refactor could consolidate by only disposing PlayerVm in the unconditional block and removing it from DisposeSubViewModels, but this is low priority.

[documentation-forward] Document the Avalonia compiled-binding DataContext/IsVisible pitfall: when you need both DataContext='{Binding SubVm}' and IsVisible='{Binding SubVm, Converter=IsNotNull}' on the same element, Avalonia's compiled-binding compiler resolves IsVisible against the DataContext type (SubVm) instead of the parent VM, causing a compile-time binding error. The fix — wrapping the view in a Panel that carries IsVisible while the inner view carries DataContext — should be documented in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md as a named pattern ('Panel-wrapper for sub-VM visibility') so future contributors know the canonical solution immediately.
